newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greece christens child of Cypriot killed in clash.
newsitem.headline: Greece christens child of Cypriot killed in clash.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos on Monday christened the infant daughter of a Greek Cypriot beaten to death by Turks or Turkish Cypriots in a symbolic gesture of solidarity to Greeks on the divided island.
"We want in this manner to express our gratitude at the struggle of the father of this small child and to honour his sacrifice," said Pangalos after christening seven-month-old Anastassia Issak.

Her father Anastassios, known as Tassos, was clubbed to death with bats and steel bars by a group of Turks or Turkish Cypriots during violent clashes last August in the United Nations-controlled buffer zone dividing Cyprus.
"I did this as the representative of the Greek government, and I believe in the name of the entire Greek nation," said Pangalos, who described it a "sacred duty".
The island has been divided since Turkish troops invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 days after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.

Hundreds of people, including Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and cabinet members, crammed into a church in the southeastern town of Paralimni to watch the emotionally charged ceremony. The christening coincided with Greek Orthodox Easter. Anastassia means resurrection in Greek.
Pangalos, a white sheet draped over his shoulder, took Anastassia and helped dress her in frilly white clothes after she was dipped into the baptism bath.

Isaak, 24, was taking part in a demonstration organised by Greek Cypriot motorcyclists against the division of the island when he was killed. People living in the Turkish-held areas of the island were holding a counter-demonstration in the same area.
